Rashi on Shabbat 34a:10:1.hebrew: ה"ג אמר רבא מפני מה אמרו אין טומנין בדבר שאינו מוסיף הבל - כגון צמר ומוכין:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:10:1.english: This is the reading: Rava said: Why did they say one may not insulate in something that does not add heat - Such as wool and flocking.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:10:2.hebrew: משחשכה - כדתנן במתניתין: ״וטומנין את החמין״ — טעמא דספק חשכה, הא ודאי חשכה אין טומנין. וסתם הטמנה — בדבר שאינו מוסיף הבל, דאילו בדבר המוסיף הבל, אפי׳ מבעוד יום אסור, כדתנן בפ״ד (דף מז:): ״אין טומנין לא בגפת כו׳״. גזירה — שמא ימצא קדרתו שנצטננה כשירצה להטמינה, וירתיחנה תחילה, ונמצא מבשל בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:10:2.english: From nightfall - As we learned in our Mishnah: “And one may insulate hot food” — the reason [it is permitted is that it is] uncertain darkness, but [if it is] definitely dark, one may not insulate. And an unspecified [mention of] insulation [is referring to] something that does not add heat, for with something that adds heat, [it is] forbidden even while it is still day, as we learned in chapter 4 (daf 47b): “One may not insulate with olive-peat, etc.” [It is] a decree lest he find that his pot has cooled down when he wants to insulate it, and he will boil it first, and thereby turn out to be cooking on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:10:3.hebrew: אי הכא בין השמשות נמי ניגזר - דהא שבות מעלייתא היא, דהא איכא גזירת איסור דאורייתא; ותנא דמתניתין אית ליה דגזרו על השבות ביה"ש, דקתני: אין מעשרין את הודאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:10:3.english: If so, during twilight we should also issue a decree - For this is a full-fledged rabbinic prohibition, as there is a decree [protecting against] a Torah prohibition; and the Tanna of our Mishnah holds that they decreed [against] rabbinic prohibitions during twilight, as he teaches: One may not tithe [produce that is] definitely untithed.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:10:4.hebrew: רותחות הן - שסמוך לביה"ש הוא מעבירם מעל האור, וליכא למיחש לשמא נצטננה וירתיחנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:10:4.english: They are boiling - For close to twilight, he removes them from upon the fire, and there is no concern that perhaps it cooled down and he will boil it.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:1:1.hebrew: ואית להו צערא לאקופי - שהיה אותו שוק שהספק בו מקום מעבר העיר לרבים, והכהנים לא היו יכולין ליכנס שם מפני טומאה, וצריך להקיף דרך אחר ארוך:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:1:1.english: And they are troubled to circumvent [it] - For that marketplace in which the doubt lay was a thoroughfare of the city for the public, and the priests were unable to enter there because of [ritual] impurity, and had to circumvent [it by] another, long way.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:1:2.hebrew: איכא דידע דאיתחזק טהרה - בהאי שוק מימיו, שלא היה בית הקברות גמור, ולא ניתן לפנותו:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:1:2.english: Is there [anyone] who knows that [a presumption of] purity was established - In this marketplace [ever] in its days, [to show] that it was not a full-fledged cemetery, [which] is not permitted to be cleared.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:1:3.english: Here ben Zakkai cut - He planted them and uprooted them after they grew.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:1:4.hebrew: תורמסי תרומה - הצריכות לשמרן בטהרה, וגם הוא היה כהן, כדאמרינן [בתוספתא דפרה] (פ"ג): אם מה שעשו ידי שכחתי:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:1:4.english: Lupines of teruma - Which must be guarded in purity; and he was also a priest, as we say [in the Tosefta of Parah] (chapter 3): “If I have forgotten what my hands did...”

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:1:5.hebrew: עבד איהו נמי הכי - היה מקצץ תורמסין ומשליכן שם, ונעשה נס וצף המת במקום שהוא שם, וציינו למקום הקבר. הכי מפרש בפסיקתא דפרשת העומר ובסדר זרעים ירושלמי:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:1:5.english: He too did so - He would cut up lupines and throw them there, and a miracle occurred and the corpse floated up in the place where it was, and he marked the place of the grave. This is explained in the Pesikta of Parashat HaOmer and in Seder Zera'im of the Yerushalmi.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:2:2.english: And you were counted - You agreed with our view to be among the count.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:2:3.english: Adorn each other - [Each one adorns] the hair of her fellow so that she will look beautiful.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:2:4.english: A pile of bones - Like a corpse whose flesh has rotted and fallen off a long time ago.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:1.hebrew: עם חשכה - שאם ימהר להזכירם מבעוד יום, יפשעו ויאמרו: עדיין יש שהות:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:1.english: At nightfall - For if he reminds them early, while it is still day, they will be negligent and say: "There is still time."

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:2.hebrew: עשרתם - פירות האילן לסעודת שבת, שאף אכילת עראי של שבת קובעת למעשר, כדאמרינן במסכת ביצה (דף לד:): דשבת עונג איקרי, מכל שהוא הוי עונג:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:2.english: Have you tithed - [Did you tithe] the fruit of the tree for the Shabbat meal? For even casual eating on Shabbat establishes [an obligation] to tithe, as we say in Tractate Beitzah (34b): For Shabbat is called "a delight," [and] even the slightest amount constitutes delight.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:3.hebrew: ערבתם - ערובי תחומין וחצירות. והני תרי שייכי למימרינהו בלשון שאלה, דשמא כבר עשו; אבל בנר לא שייך "הדלקתם", דדבר הנראה לעין הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:3.english: Have you placed the eiruv? - [This refers to] the eiruvin of [Shabbat] boundaries and [of] courtyards. And these two are appropriate to be stated in the form of a question, for perhaps they have already done [so]; but regarding the lamp, [asking] “Have you lit?” is not applicable, as it is a matter visible to the eye.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:4.hebrew: ספק חשכה - כגון בין השמשות. אין מעשרין את הודאי — דתיקון מעליא הוא; אע"ג דשבות בעלמא היא, קסבר: גזרו על השבות אף על בהש"מ:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:4.english: Uncertainty whether it is nightfall - Such as twilight [bein hashemashot]. “One may not tithe definite [produce]” — because it is a substantial rectification; although it is merely a rabbinic restriction [shevut], he holds that they decreed against a rabbinic restriction even during twilight.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:5.hebrew: ואין מטבילין את הכלים - דהוי נמי שבות, כדאמרינן במסכת ביצה (דף יח.), דנראה כמתקן כלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:5.english: And one may not immerse vessels - For it is also a rabbinic prohibition [shevut], as we say in Tractate Beitzah (18a), that it appears like repairing a vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:6.hebrew: ואין מדליקין את הנרות - כ"ש, דספיקא דאורייתא היא, ו"זו ואין צריך לומר זו" קתני:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:6.english: And one may not light the lamps - [This is] all the more so, as it is a doubt concerning a Torah [prohibition]; and [the Mishnah] teaches [in the manner of] "this, and it goes without saying that."

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:7.hebrew: אבל מעשרין את הדמאי - דלא דמי למתקן, דרוב ע"ה מעשרין הן:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:7.english: However, one may tithe demai - For it does not resemble fixing [an item], since the majority of the common people tithe.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:8.hebrew: ומערבין - עירוב. ובגמרא פריך: הא תנן לעיל ״עם חשכה ערבתם״ — מקמי דליהוי ספק:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:8.english: And one may place an eiruv - [Meaning establishing an] eiruv. And in the Gemara it asks: Didn't we learn above, 'At nightfall: Have you placed an eiruv?' — before there is uncertainty!

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:9.hebrew: וטומנין את החמין - נותנן בקופה של מוכין, להיות חומם משתמר בהן. אבל משחשכה ודאי — אין טומנין בהן, כדמפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:3:9.english: And one may insulate the hot [water] - One places them in a basket of sheared wool so that their heat will be preserved in them. But once it has definitely grown dark, one may not insulate in them, as is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:5:1.hebrew: עם חשכה - מבעוד יום הוא, ויש שהות לעשר ולערב:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:5:1.english: At nightfall - It is while it is still day, and there is time to tithe and to make an eiruv.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:7:1.hebrew: בעירובי תחומין - תיקון מעליא, דאסמכוה רבנן תחומין אקראי, ואפי' למאן דאמר תחומין דרבנן, כדאמרינן בעירובין (דף נא.): ילפינן מקום ממקום ומקום מניסה כו'. אבל עירובי חצרות — חומרא בעלמא הוא, ולא מיקרי שביתה מעלייתא, וספקא דבין השמשות שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:7:1.english: Regarding the joining of Shabbat boundaries - [It is] a substantial enactment, for the Sages based [the prohibition of leaving] boundaries on verses, and even according to the one who says [that Shabbat] boundaries are rabbinic, as we say in Eruvin (51a): “We derive ‘place’ from ‘place,’ and ‘place’ from flight,” etc. However, the joining of courtyards is merely a stringency, and is not called a full-fledged [establishment of] Shabbat residence; and [in a case of] uncertainty at twilight, it is well permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:8:1.english: [At] twilight an eiruv takes effect - For it is the beginning of the sanctity of the day.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:8:2.english: Was eaten - That a dog or a person ate it.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:8:3.hebrew: שעירב עליו מבעוד יום - הניח עירוב לסוף התחום מבעוד יום, ולא הספיק להחשיך ממש עד שנאכל בין השמשות:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:8:3.english: [The one] for whom he placed an eiruv while it was still day - He placed an eiruv at the end of the [Shabbat] boundary while it was still day, and it had not yet become truly dark before it was eaten during twilight.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:8:4.hebrew: שניהם קנו עירוב - דלגבי האי שנאכל בין השמשות, משוינן ליה ליליא, ואמרינן: כבר קדש היום בעוד העירוב קיים, וקנה עירוב — דהלכה כר' יוסי, דאמר בעירובין (דף לה.): ספק עירוב כשר. ולגבי דהאי שהונח עליו בין השמשות ונתקיים עד שחשכה, משוינן לבין השמשות יממא, ועדיין לא קדש היום כשהונח, ונמצא שהיה שם כבר בשעת קניית עירוב:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:8:4.english: Both of them acquired an eiruv - For regarding this one whose [eiruv] was eaten during twilight, we treat it as night, and we say: The day had already become sanctified while the eiruv was intact, and he acquired an eiruv — as the halakhah follows Rabbi Yose, who said in Eruvin (35a): An uncertain eiruv is valid. And regarding that one for whom it was placed during twilight and remained intact until nightfall, we treat twilight as day, and the day had not yet become sanctified when it was placed; and it turns out that it was already there at the time the eiruv was acquired.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:9:1.english: Let the latter one acquire [his eiruv] - This is the one for whom [the eiruv] was placed during twilight.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:9:2.english: Let the first [one] not acquire - For behold, it was eaten while it was still day.

Rashi on Shabbat 34a:9:3.hebrew: ה"ג ספקא דרבנן היא - כלומר, הא מילתא דמספקא לן — אי בין השמשות יממא או ליליא — במילתא דרבנן איתרע לן, בעירובי תחומין דרבנן, וכל ספקא דרבנן לקולא:
Rashi on Shabbat 34a:9:3.english: This is the reading: It is a rabbinic uncertainty - That is to say, this matter that is uncertain to us — whether twilight is day or night — occurred to us in a rabbinic matter, [namely] in an eiruv of boundaries, which is rabbinic; and any rabbinic uncertainty [is ruled] leniently.

Tosafot on Shabbat 34a:1:1.hebrew: עבד איהו נמי הכי - מפר"ת: כמו יעקב אבינו, ותיקן מילתא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 34a:1:1.english: "He also did so" - Rabbeinu Tam explains: Like Jacob our forefather, and he instituted an improvement.

Tosafot on Shabbat 34a:1:2.hebrew: כל היכא דהוה קשי טהריה - כדאיתא בנדה בפרק האשה (דף סא. ושם), דתניא: אמר רבי יוסי בן שאול, מעשה בסלע שהיו מחזיקין בה טומאה, כו'. אמר להו: "הביאו לי סדינין!" הביאו לו, ושראן במים ופרסו עליו; מקום טומאה — לח, מקום טהרה — נגוב:
Tosafot on Shabbat 34a:1:2.english: "Everywhere that was hard, he pronounced it ritually pure" - As it is stated in Niddah in the chapter [entitled] Ha'isha (61a, and see there), as it is taught [in a baraita]: Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said: There was an incident involving bedrock regarding which they held a presumption of ritual impurity, etc. [Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya] said to them: "Bring me sheets." They brought [them] to him, and he soaked them in water and spread them over it: [any] place of ritual impurity [remained] moist, [and any] place of ritual purity [remained] dry.

Tosafot on Shabbat 34a:7:1.hebrew: לא קשיא כאן בעירובי תחומין כו' - נראה לר"ת כפירוש הקונטרס, דבעירובי תחומין מחמרינן משום דאית להו סמך מן המקרא; וכן פר"ח, וכן יש בירושלמי. וכן משמע בפרק מי שהוציאוהו (עירובין דף מו: וסם) גבי הא דקאמר: "הלכה כדברי המיקל בעירוב", רב פפא אמר: איצטריך, סד"א ה"מ עירובי חצרות, אבל בעירובי תחומין אימא לא. ומעיקרא היה מפרש ר"ת דעירובי חצרות חמירי טפי, דאין מערבין אלא בפת, כדמשמע בפרק הדר (עירובין דף עא:) ובחלון (שם דף פא. ושם); אבל בעירובי תחומין מערבין בכל דבר חוץ ממים ומלח. ואין נראה, דהא ר"מ ס"ל דתחומין דאורייתא בפרק בכל מערבין (עירובין לה.), ואפ"ה אית ליה בהדר דעירובי חצרות בפת ובעירובי תחומין מערבין בכל דבר, דלא אשכחן דפליג ר"מ אסתם משנה דבכל מערבין. וטעמא דמקילי בתחומים דלא בעי פת — משום דאין מערבין אלא לדבר מצוה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 34a:7:1.english: "It is not difficult; here [it refers] to eiruvei teḥumin, etc." - It appears to Rabbeinu Tam like the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], that regarding eiruvei teḥumin we are stringent because they have support from Scripture; and so explained Rabbeinu Ḥananel, and so it is found in the Yerushalmi. And so it is implied in the chapter [entitled] "Mi SheHotzi’uhu" (Eruvin 46b and there) regarding that which [the Gemara] states: "The halakhah follows the words of the one who is lenient with regard to an eiruv," [whereupon] Rav Pappa said: It was necessary [to state this explicitly, for] you might have thought to say: This applies only to eiruvei ḥatzerot, but with regard to eiruvei teḥumin I might say no [it does not]. And originally, Rabbeinu Tam would explain that eiruvei ḥatzerot are more stringent, since one may establish an eiruv only with bread, as is implied in the chapter [entitled] "Hadar" (Eruvin 71b) and in [the chapter entitled] "BaḤalon" (ibid. 81a and there); whereas regarding eiruvei teḥumin, one may establish an eiruv with anything except water and salt. But this does not appear [correct], for Rabbi Meir holds that [the prohibition of leaving the Shabbat] boundary is from the Torah in the chapter [entitled] "Bekhol Me'arvin" (Eruvin 35a), and even so, he holds in "Hadar" that eiruvei ḥatzerot [must be established] with bread, while for eiruvei teḥumin one may establish an eiruv with anything, since we do not find that Rabbi Meir disputes the anonymous Mishnah in "Bekhol Me'arvin". And the reason that they are lenient regarding [Shabbat] boundaries that it does not require bread is because one establishes an eiruv [of boundaries] only for the purpose of a mitzvah.

Tosafot on Shabbat 34a:8:1.hebrew: נאכל עירובו משחשכה - לאו דווקא, וה"ה לא נאכל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 34a:8:1.english: His eiruv was eaten after nightfall - [This is] not specifically [so], and the same applies [even if] it was not eaten.

Tosafot on Shabbat 34a:8:2.hebrew: שניהם קנו עירוב - פירש בקונטרס: דרבא איירי בעירובי תחומין, וכן משמע לשון "צא וערב". ואע"פ דספק חשכה אין מערבין עירובי תחומין — ה"מ לכתחילה, אבל בדיעבד כשר, כר' יוסי, דאמר (עירובין פ"ג דף לה.): "ספק עירוב כשר". וקשה לרשב"א: דר' יוסי לית ליה התם, גבי נפל עליו גל או נשרף או תרומה ונטמאה, ספק עירוב [כשר] אלא משום חזקה, כדתניא התם בהדיא (דף לו.): "כיצד אמר רבי יוסי ספק עירוב כשר" כו'; אבל בספק כי הכא, שהניחו בין השמשות או נאכל בין השמשות — לא מכשר! ומפר"ת: דהכא מיירי בעירובי חצרות; וכן פר"ח; וכן מוכח בסוף הדר (עירובין דף עו.). ו"צא" אשכחן נמי דלאו חוץ לעיר קאמר, כמו: "צא ושכור לנו פועלים" (ב"מ דף פג.):
Tosafot on Shabbat 34a:8:2.english: Both of them acquired the eiruv - Rashi explained that Rava is dealing with an eiruv techumin [the boundary eiruv], and this is also indicated by the phrasing "Go out and place an eiruv." And even though [the rule is that at] a time of uncertain darkness one may not establish an eiruv techumin, this applies only ab initio [lekhathilah]; however, ex post facto [bedi'avad] it is valid, in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, who said (Eruvin, chapter 3, 35b): "An eiruv [whose validity is] in doubt is valid." And the Rashba questioned this: for Rabbi Yosei maintains there — in a case where a rockslide fell upon it, or it was burned, or [it was] terumah that became ritually impure — that an eiruv [whose validity is] in doubt [is valid] only because of a legal presumption [chazakah], as it is explicitly taught there (36a): "In what case did Rabbi Yosei say that an eiruv in doubt is valid?..." etc.; however, in a case of doubt like this here, where he placed it during twilight or it was eaten during twilight, he does not validate it! Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam explains that here [Rava] is dealing with an eiruv chatzerot [the joining of courtyards]. And so explained Rabbeinu Chananel. And this is also proven at the end of [the chapter entitled] Hadar (Eruvin 76a). And as for [the expression] "go out," we also find that it does not mean [going] outside the city, as in: "Go out and hire workers for us" (Bava Metzia 83a).
